newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian shares drop as volume plummets.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian shares drop as volume plummets.

text.p: Palestinian shares closed down on Sunday as the volume of trading on the Palestine Securities Exchange (PSE) plunged after a Moslem religious holiday.

The Jerusalem index closed at 100.37, down from 100.49 on Wednesday. About 80,776 shares worth 130,301 Jordanian dinars changed hands, down from 222,884 shares worth 356,172 dinars traded on Wednesday.
"It was a quiet day, a dull day," said Safwan Bataina, PSE general manager, adding the number of working days was shortened because of the Prophet Mohammad's birthday.
"Thursday was a holiday, but the deeper reason I think is the continuation of this stalemate on the political front," he said.

Palestinian-Israeli peace talks have been frozen since March when Israel broke ground on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem. Israel claims Jerusalem as its eternal capital, but Palestinians want the eastern part as capital of a future state.
"It's making people lose interest in investment. People are waiting to see if there's going to be any development on the political front," Bataina said.
"The economic situation is keeping investors on the sidelines in the waiting mode," he said.
In trading this week, the Palestine Telecommunication Co, which accounted for 82 percent of the total turnover, closed even at 1.45 dinars per share.

The National Insurance Co fell one percent to 1.98 dinars per share, and the Jerusalem Pharmaceutical Co dropped 1.69 percent to 5.80 dinars per share. The Arab Insurance Establishment dropped 0.67 percent to 2.96 dinars a share.
Seven other companies showed no changes.
Trading is conducted in dollars or Jordanian dinars in the absence of a Palestinian currency.
